title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (5.1%)
drivers.evidence: Price rose to 4.56 from 4.34. Past same-price week (2026-09-28) sold baseline units. Higher prices reduce demand, especially without promotion.

drivers.name: Supplier delivery short
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates supply risk. This is a direct demand constraint, not just a price effect. Likely reduces sales below baseline.

adjustment.analysis: Halloween has historically had no uplift (noise-adjusted x1.0), and past promotions show mixed effects. The current 5.1% price increase is above prior promotions (max 30% off), but price hikes reduce demand. The recent week with the same price (2026-09-28) sold 207 units (baseline 207.6), showing no lift. The supplier warning of short delivery suggests supply risk, likely reducing sales. No evidence of demand spike from price or event. The baseline trend is slightly negative (-4.6% 13-week), but not strong enough to override. Adjust down for price and supply risk.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.6 - 290.2 | 10%-90%: 156.4 - 281.0

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
